text.tspan: An ideal gas is taken through an isobaric compression, as shown in the pressure-volume diagram. Which of the
following claims is correct about the direction of the energy transfer, if any, between the gas and its surroundings
(A)Heat energy is transferred from the surroundings to the gas.
(B)Heat energy is transferred from the gas to the surroundings.
(C)There is no transfer of heat energy.
(D)It cannot be determined without knowing whether the gas is insulated.
Correct. Energy is transferred via heating from the gas to the environment as the gas is being compressed
to keep the gas at constant pressure.
